headline: Asked the Mayor to name a lead department for e-motos and consider them for the Mayor's legislative agenda.
summary: Staff believes education and signage efforts have discouraged e-moto use on the bike path. Discussion covered new ordinance definitions, ticketing by non-police staff, and speed limits for sidewalks and the bike path. Local Motion supports most changes but opposes lowering the sidewalk riding age until infrastructure improves.
decisions: Asked the Mayor to designate a coordinating official or department to lead on e-motos and related vehicle issues, unanimously.
Asked the Mayor's Office to consider adding e-motos to the Mayor's legislative agenda, unanimously.

E-motos on the Mayor's legislative agenda
plain_text:
Ordinance Committee 
Wednesday, October 28, 2026 
Bushor Conference Room, City Hall 
or Remote via Zoom. Burlington, Vermont 
DRAFT MINUTES 
 
 
Members Present: Councilor Bergman (Chair), Councilor Barlow, Councilor Carpenter 
 
Staff Present: Kim Sturtevant (Assistant City Attorney), Phillip Peterson (Senior Transportation 
Planner), Phil Lewis (Director of Parks, Recreation, & Waterfront), Jonathan Young (BPD 
Deputy Chief of Operations), Victor Prussack (Burlington School District Engagement Director) 
 
Public Present: Sharon Bushor, Jack Evans (Local Motion) 
 
Meeting called to order at 4:02 PM. 
 
1. Adopt the Agenda 
1.01 Adopt the Agenda 
 
Motion to Adopt Agenda. 
 
Motion by Councilor Barlow, Seconded by Councilor Carpenter 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
2. Adopt Draft Minutes 
2.01 Adopt Draft Minutes from October 13, 2026 
 
Motion to Adopt minutes October 13, 2026. 
 
Motion by Councilor Barlow, Seconded by Councilor Carpenter 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
3. Public Forum 
3.01 Verbal Comments 
 
Sharon Bushor commented on the attachments included with the meeting agenda, noting the 
DMV flyer is informative but not easy to understand.  Bushor also suggested several outreach 
and engagement ideas to include more community partners and reach schools.  Bushor added 
enforcement should elevate awareness for children and their families and expressed being in 
support of reducing the age from 16 to 12 for sidewalk riding, emphasizing the pedestrian  needs 
to be remembered in this process.
Public Forum closed at 4:13 PM.  
 
4.  E-Moto Discussion 
4.01 E-Moto Discussion 
 
Motion to request the Mayor designate a coordinating official or department, noting the 
Department of Public Works’ offer, to take lead on e-motos and other related vehicular issues.   
Motion by Councilor Carpenter, Seconded by Councilor Barlow 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
Motion staff to communicate to Mayor’s Office to consider adding e-motos to the Mayor’s 
legislative agenda.  
Motion by Councilor Carpenter, Seconded by Councilor Barlow 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
Discussion: 
 
The Committee heard from the Department of Public Works, Burlington Parks, Recreation, & 
Waterfront, Burlington Police Department, Burlington School District, and Local Motion on e-
motos.  
 
• Senior Transportation Planner Peterson updated the Committee: 
o DPW partnered with BPRW, BSD, and BPD on education campaigns and 
outreach, updated signage, and continues to research how other municipalities are 
approaching the problem 
o Anecdotally believes these efforts have deterred e-moto use on the bike path 
o Advised there are no operational rules for congestion zones and no enforcement 
authority for non-sworn City staff 
o Noted DPW recommends clarifying definitions in BCO Chapter 6, clarifying aim 
of e-moto ordinance changes, implementing less punitive enforcement 
approaches, that DPW is prepared to collaborate across departments and move 
this initiative forward, and that City Council acknowledge existing conditions at 
the state level allowing vendors to sell e-motos to minors 
 
• Deputy Chief Young corroborated Peterson’s report of less e-moto activity and 
emphasized education and outreach must work in conjunction with enforcement.  DC 
Young stated enforcing speed limits on the bike path would be challenging and 
recommended CSOs and other non-sworn staff have the authority to ticket violators.
• BSD Engagement Director Prussack added BSD started hosting advisory groups to 
involve students in the conversation and continues to gather data on how many students 
use alternative transportation to get to school.  Prussack offered to facilitate the 
Committee meeting with student groups.   
 
• BPRW Director Lewis stated BPRW focused on engagement, with positive results via 
social media campaigns, and updating signage for the bike path and recommends the 
ordinance clarify e-motos are not allowed in parks or the bike path.   
 
• Jack Evans with Local Motion expressed the organization is in support of the majority of 
changes identified, but noted Local Motion has concerns about the impact of 
impoundment, ordinance definitions, and the City’s ability to set and enforce speed limits 
on bike paths.  Evans suggested the ordinance definitions create a new definition that 
would capture all non-compliant devices not explicitly defined in ordinance.  Evans 
mentioned Local Motion’s voucher program for e-bikes was effective and the City could 
implement something similar to address the e-moto issue, and also commented Local 
Motion does not support lowering the sidewalk age for riding until the City improves 
transportation infrastructure for riders and pedestrians.   
 
The Committee discussed potential changes to the ordinance: 
 
• Councilor Barlow noted the definitions should distinguish between devices traveling on 
roadways versus shared use paths and voiced support for Local Motion’s request for a 
definition to capture any device not explicitly defined.  Attorney Sturtevant explained the 
definitions classify devices by how fast they can go, not how fast they are allowed to go.  
Local Motion added federal regulations reflect high-powered and low-powered devices, 
with the determining threshold being 20 mph and recommends removing language 
dictating a device’s design to future-proof definitions.  Peterson clarified the 25 mph in 
the motor-assisted micromobility device definition comes from the state’s transportation 
laws.  Chair Bergman noted the Committee should consider how changes to the 
definitions may affect provisions in Section 6-3.   
 
• Councilor Barlow proposed putting a speed limit on sidewalk travel for those who can 
ride bikes on the sidewalk.  Chair Bergman suggested Section 6-3(a) might be an 
appropriate place to add a speed limit and requested the relevant departments advise on 
an appropriate limit and identify other limits to consider setting.   
 
• The Committee questioned if the provisions of Section 6-3(b) meet the criteria for a 
trespass, and whether that would be a civil or criminal violation.   
 
• Chair Bergman flagged Section 6-3(e) to be considered with any changes related to speed 
limits.
• The Committee determined Section 6-3(g) might also be a place for amendments 
expanding on sidewalk prohibitions.  Peterson noted there should be ADA language in 
that section.  Attorney Sturtevant explained the difference between Sections 6-3(g) and 
proposed amendment 6-3(i).  Chair Bergman requested Section 6-3(i) be integrated into 
Section 6-3(g).   
 
5. Any Other Committee Business 
5.01 Any Other Committee Business 
 
The Committee set the next meeting for Friday, November 6, 2026 at 2:00 PM.  The next 
collaborative IZ meeting with Planning Commission will be November 18, 2026.  The Ordinance 
Committee will meet a second time in November on November 19, 2026.  The Committee 
discussed the potential agenda items for each meeting.   
 
6. Adjournment 
6.01 Motion to Adjourn 
 
The meeting was adjourned with no objection by Chair Bergman at 5:40 PM.
